title: Nouns and articles
intro: de or het, een or nothing, plurals, little words with -je, and long compound words.

topics.title: de and het
topics.summary: Two words for ‘the’. Every plural takes de.

body.p: Dutch has two words for ‘the’: **de** and **het**. About two out of three nouns are de-words. In the **plural every noun takes de**.

list: Small words ending in -je (diminutives): **het meisje**, **het huisje**, **het kopje**
A verb used as a noun: **het eten**, **het leven**
Most words ending in -um, -ment, -isme: **het museum**, **het document**
Most words starting with ge-, be-, ver-, ont- (no extra ending): **het gesprek**, **het begin**, **het verhaal**, **het ontbijt**
People and jobs: **de man**, **de vrouw**, **de dokter** (but **het kind**, **het meisje**)
Words ending in -heid, -ing, -tie, -teit, -ij: **de gezondheid**, **de woning**, **de informatie**, **de universiteit**, **de bakkerij**

body.tip: For all other nouns, learn de or het together with the word: not ‘huis’ but ‘het huis’. If you have to guess, guess **de**.

body.p: Why it matters: de or het decides **deze/dit**, **die/dat**, the adjective ending (een groot huis, een grote auto) and **die/dat** in relative clauses.

mistakes.why: Words for people are de-words (except het kind, het meisje).
Words ending in -je are always het.

exercises.why: ge- words without an extra ending are usually het.

write: Write two sentences about things in your house. Use de and het.

topics.title: een, één and no article
topics.summary: een = a/an. No article for plurals, uncountables and jobs.

body.p: **een** means ‘a’ or ‘an’. It is the same for de-words and het-words: **een man**, **een huis**. It is pronounced like a short ‘un’.
**één** with accents means the number **one**: Ik heb **één** kind.

list: Plurals in general: Ik heb **boeken**. (I have books.)
Things you cannot count: Ik drink **koffie**. Ik heb **geld**.
Jobs and nationality after zijn/worden: Ik ben **leraar**. Zij is **Marokkaans**. Hij wordt **kok**.

ex: Er staan stoelen in de kamer.
There are chairs in the room.

mistakes.why: No een before a job after zijn.

exercises.why: No article before a job after zijn.
The number one is written één.
een = a. It is not about the number here.

topics.title: Plurals
topics.summary: Mostly -en, sometimes -s or -'s, a few irregular.

body.p: Most nouns get **-en**, with the spelling rules: **de boek → boeken**, **de kat → katten**, **de straat → straten**, **het huis → huizen**.

list: Words ending in unstressed **-el, -em, -en, -er, -je**: tafel**s**, bezem**s**, jongen**s**, kamer**s**, meisje**s**
Many loanwords: de film**s**, de computer**s**

body.p: After a long **a, i, o, u, y** at the end of a word: **auto's**, **foto's**, **menu's**, **taxi's**, **baby's**. The apostrophe keeps the vowel long.

mistakes.why: Without the apostrophe you would read a short o.

exercises.why: After a long o at the end: -'s.
Irregular: the a changes to e.

topics.title: Diminutives: -je
topics.summary: huisje, kopje, balletje: small, friendly, and always het.

body.p: Dutch uses small forms a lot, not only for small things but also to sound friendly or casual: **een kopje koffie**, **een biertje**, **even een rondje lopen**. A diminutive is **always a het-word** and the plural takes **-s**: het boekje, de boekjes.

head: ending
when
examples
rows: after a vowel; after l, n, r, w with a long vowel; after unstressed -el, -en, -er
auto → auto**tje**, stoel → stoel**tje**, tafel → tafel**tje**
after m with a long vowel, or -lm, -rm
after l, m, n, r, ng with a short stressed vowel
bal → bal**letje**, man → man**netje**, ring → ring**etje**

exercises.why: Short stressed vowel + l: -etje, with double l.

topics.title: Compound nouns
topics.summary: Words are glued together; the last part decides de or het.

body.p: Dutch writes compound nouns as **one word**: **het fietspad** (bike path), **de huisdeur** (front door), **het ziekenhuis** (hospital).
The **last part** decides the article: de fiets + **het** pad = **het** fietspad; het huis + **de** deur = **de** huisdeur.
Sometimes **-s-** or **-en-** goes in between: **het stadhuis**, **het verkeersbord**, **de kippensoep**, **de pannenkoek**. Learn these with the word.
When two vowels meet and could be read wrongly, use a hyphen: **zee-egel**, **auto-ongeluk**.

mistakes.why: pad is a het-word, and the last part decides.
Compounds are written as one word.

exercises.why: A hyphen separates o + o so you read it correctly.
